prompt:
An original illustration of a court figure for a traditional European playing card, drawn fresh in the spirit of 19th-century card patterns.

Drawing: clean flat colour areas with bold, even, dark outlines of one consistent weight. No gradients, shading, texture, paper grain or engraving hatching. Simple, clear shapes and a calm, frontal, symmetrical pose, so the figure stays readable when the whole card is only 60 pixels wide.

Colour: a balanced palette of royal blue, forest green, golden yellow, deep red, black, white and a warm skin tone. No single colour dominates the costume; the colours are distributed evenly across the figure.

Background: fully transparent.

Never include text, letters, numbers, signatures, corner indices, a card border or a frame. This is an original drawing, not a copy or tracing of any existing commercial deck.

Format: portrait, the back of a playing card, used for every card of both decks. A symmetrical traditional ornament (a fine lattice or interlace with a central rosette), point-symmetric so it looks the same when the card is turned, covering the whole picture edge to edge. Only two colours: dark charcoal grey and white. No figures, no suit symbols, no text, no logo. Opaque background. This overrides the palette and the transparent background above.

Subject: the card back.
